sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Himalayan Region, 1000 to 1400 A.D.
sources.note: Direct institutional chronology. Used for monastic renewal, Atisha circa 1042 and approximate Sakya/Mongol period. Its paragraph conflates Sakya Pandita’s patron with Khubilai; that specific assertion is deliberately not reproduced.

sources.title: Roberto Vitali, Murals at Toling Dukhang: Ornament of the World, Project Himalayan Art (2023)
sources.note: Academic museum essay and attached Pakmodru glossary: Changchup Gyeltsen gained central Tibet in 1354; power faded with fifteenth-century internal conflict.

sources.title: Shengnan Dong, Gyantse Kumbum, Project Himalayan Art (2023)
sources.note: Academic museum study of the monument, its regional patrons, 1427 to 1442 construction and 73 chapels.

sources.title: Charles Ramble, Bon Deity Trowo Tsochok Khagying, Project Himalayan Art (2023)
sources.note: Academic study of a fifteenth-century painting, Met 2018.890, and organized Bon’s development in the tenth and eleventh centuries.

sources.title: Natasha N. Kimmet, Potala Palace: A Monument of Tibetan Cultural Identity, Project Himalayan Art (2023)
sources.note: Direct academic museum essay. Government institutions, palace dates, conscripted labor and Ganden Podrang’s 1642 to 1959 central Tibetan history; not evidence of unchanged sovereignty throughout that interval.

sources.title: Treasury of Lives, 18th Century
sources.note: Full English original accessed through indexed Spanish-locale page. Used for 1717 invasion, 1720 expulsion and 1727 ambans. Avoids its anachronistic Qinghai province wording.

sources.title: Theresia Hofer, Desi Sanggye Gyatso’s Medical Paintings, Project Himalayan Art (2023)
sources.note: Academic study: original designs 1687 to 1697; many illustrated witnesses are twentieth-century copies. Distinguishes Chakpori founded 1696 from later Mentsikhang. Plates 5, 22, 49 and 64 support specific daily-life and diagnostic examples.

sources.title: Treasury of Lives, Samding Dorje Pakmo incarnation line
sources.note: Institutional scholarly account of Chokyi Dronma’s marriage, child, ordination and female reincarnation lineage. No universal claim about women’s opportunities.

sources.title: Andrew Quintman, Earliest Extant Printed Edition of Milarepa’s Life Story, Project Himalayan Art (2023)
sources.note: Direct scholarly study of the 1538 print at Ron Wosel Puk in Gungtang. Earliest surviving edition of this biography, not earliest Tibetan printing.

sources.title: Grolier Club and Rare Book School, The Four Medical Tantras, item 2798
sources.note: Direct collection catalogue: Tibetan title and transliteration, circa 1750 copy probably Beijing; robe and belt terminology for wrapper and cord. Sample is the catalogue’s original-language title transcription, not claimed to have been read from a photographed leaf.

sources.title: Tsering Namgyal, The Fifth Panchen Lama, Lobzang Yeshe, Treasury of Lives
sources.note: Full indexed scholarly biography read. Used for childhood reading/writing tutor and late 1720s smallpox precautions. Page explains competing Panchen numbering; follows its Tashilhunpo fifth designation.

sources.title: ICOMOS, Norbulingka evaluation, World Heritage nominations (2001), printed pages 57 to 59
sources.note: Direct PDF text, human PDF pages 62 to 64. Construction chronology is in History and Description; seasonal government move is in the reproduced State Party justification. No modern political formula projected backward.

proposedOverrides.name: Tibet
proposedOverrides.summary: Tibetan regional societies, religious institutions and governments across a changing medieval and early modern plateau.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Broad historical-basemaps Tibet record; regional narrative, not one unchanging polity.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 13 snapshots, total bounds approximately 77.241 to 103.204 E and 26.284 to 38.961 N; see identities.json. Outline encompasses areas outside individual central Tibetan governments’ effective authority.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Circa 1250 used as approximate Sakya predominance boundary; 1354, 1642 and 1720 mark central Tibetan political transitions. No claim that these phases precisely match every imported polygon.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Catalogue-attested Tibetan medical title from a circa 1750 copy probably Beijing; not a newly invented sentence or a claim of direct reading from the photographed folio.
